### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a731859def47e2c8cefcab4d635a1c45c60c2c1` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2113393e6464a0287a5822d2c7ce8f4a3dd287f6` — the merge of head `dc8f1abe60d3f9b070197b9f02a8ebf904401f95` into base `6a731859def47e2c8cefcab4d635a1c45c60c2c1`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2113393e6464a0287a5822d2c7ce8f4a3dd287f6 && git checkout 2113393e6464a0287a5822d2c7ce8f4a3dd287f6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 6a731859def47e2c8cefcab4d635a1c45c60c2c1 dc8f1abe60d3f9b070197b9f02a8ebf904401f95 && git checkout -B drift-repro 6a731859def47e2c8cefcab4d635a1c45c60c2c1 && git merge --no-ff dc8f1abe60d3f9b070197b9f02a8ebf904401f95

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 6a731859def47e2c8cefcab4d635a1c45c60c2c1
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dc8f1abe60d3f9b070197b9f02a8ebf904401f95`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts + none

Inputs read: card #35698 (body, triage 7026722554, claim 7097848971, dev report 7098411542; no ruling and no earlier record on the thread), PR #36666 (body, 4-file list, net diff against `main`), and the check-runs on this head. Remainder of the diff, the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`: `.changeset/35698-text-key-literal-close.md`, `packages/spec/src/data/hook-texts.test.ts`, `packages/spec/src/ui/action-texts.test.ts`. Code read outside the diff, not reviewed: `packages/spec/src/data/hook.zod.ts` (`refuseUndeclaredLiteralTextKey`), `packages/spec/src/ui/action.zod.ts` (`refuseUndeclaredLiteralActionTextKey`), `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-text.ts` (`buildDeclaredTextSurface`), `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`.

### ① Derived judgments

- Accept set, save doors of `HookSchema` and `ActionSchema` (the only two callers of `hookTextKeysAskedIn`, at `hook.zod.ts:363` and `action.zod.ts:2687`): WIDER by exactly the bodies whose `ctx.text(` or `ctx.text?.(` first argument opens with a quoted snake_case key and continues past the closing quote with anything other than whitespace, a comment, `,` or `)`. Right: that set is the computed keys, and each was refused at save for a key the body never asks for.
- Refusal set kept: every body where the quoted key is the whole first argument is refused as on `main`, same path (`body.source` or `handler`), same sentence (`undeclaredHookTextKeyAtSave`, `undeclaredActionTextKeyAtSave` untouched). Right.
- Run-time half unchanged and real on both owners: `buildDeclaredTextSurface` throws `owner.undeclaredAtRun(key, declared)` for any key `texts` does not own, wired to `undeclaredHookTextAtRun` and `undeclaredActionTextAtRun`. A body newly accepted at save is therefore still refused, naming the built key, when the built key is undeclared. Right.
- Public surface: no export added, removed or retyped; `TEXT_CALL` is module-private; no schema shape, `.describe()` or error sentence moved. The three docblock hunks are prose on a published file and agree with the code (④). Right. `Spec property liveness`, `Lint · docs & code guards`, `Type Check · source gates`, `Flag docs affected by code changes` all concluded success on this head.
- Published prose elsewhere stays true without an edit: the `texts` `.describe()` on both schemas ("at save when the hook asks for it literally, otherwise at run time") and `hooks.mdx` ("if the hook names it literally in `ctx.text('key')` or `ctx.text?.('key')`, otherwise when the hook runs"). Right.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. A bug fix in a released package; nothing an author can write as metadata is added, removed or re-meant. `Check Changeset` concluded success.
- Clause-②: no — holds. The diff does accept at save a body `main` refused, so the question is whether the published text had promised that refusal. It had not; it had promised the opposite, three times on `main`: the `hookTextKeysAskedIn` docblock ("A key that arrives any other way (a variable, a computed value) is left to the run-time refusal"), the `texts` `.describe()` on both schemas, and `hooks.mdx`. `'follow_up' + suffix` is a computed value under every one of them. The only `main` text that could be read the other way is the private `TEXT_CALL` docblock, which shows the open prefix `ctx.text('key'` and says both shapes "ask for the key literally"; that sentence describes the two call shapes, not what may follow the quote, and it is not a published promise. The save now matches the published contract; the contract did not move. No `(widening)` arm is owed.
- PR body and changeset carry the same two declaration lines.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty.
- Dev flag, out-of-scope finding (class b): `CODE_PROPERTY`, `CODE_ASSIGNMENT`, `REASON_PROPERTY`, `REASON_ASSIGNMENT` stop at the closing quote the same way. Confirmed on the head: all four end at the back-reference to their opening quote with nothing after it, against the `hookRefusalCodesThrownIn` docblock. Answered: correctly not folded in, since a property and an assignment end differently from a call argument; it is owed ONE family card from the seat, not a change on this head.
- Dev flag, declared narrowing of the local gate set (67 of 85 derived families unrun locally): answered by the check-runs on this head, every one success or skipped, `Governed Surface Queue Guard` and `Lint · PM dispatch-gates` included.
- Dev deviations (trailer amended before first push; PR body line order; attribution footer form): process notes, no effect on the contract; the lane seat's.
- SQL push-down: not applicable. The diff is one regular expression and prose; no query, no id materialisation, no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts`, against the card's ask, ruling 6913660232 parameter 7 as the section header cites it, and its two consumers.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

Attempts to break the lookahead `(?=\s*[,)])`:

- A literal ask `main` refused that the head lets through: none found in valid JavaScript. After a first argument that is one string literal, the grammar allows only whitespace, a comment, `,` or `)`. Whitespace of every kind is `\s`, line and paragraph separators and the byte-order mark included. A block comment and a line comment are blanked by `maskedSource` in scan order with their line breaks kept, so `'key' /* don't */)`, `'key' // it's\n)` and `'key'\n// note\n, params` all still match; a quote inside such a comment cannot desynchronise the string scan because the comment is consumed whole first. A trailing comma `('key',)` matches. `'key' as const` and `'key'!` are TypeScript, erased before `Function.prototype.toString()` and a syntax error in a `js` body.
- A computed key still read as literal: none introduced. A comment that hides an operator is blanked and the operator after it is then seen (`'key' /* x */ + suffix`, `'key' // x\n + suffix`, `'key'\n.concat(suffix)`, `'key'\n[0]` all fail the lookahead). `'a' + 'b'` keeps both literals under the masking exception and fails on `+`.
- Masking against the docblock's claims: "a comment is blanked to whitespace first" is true, newlines survive and are whitespace. "a template with a `${}` hole is never kept as a literal by the masking at all" is true for every hole: `$` and `{` are outside both kept patterns, so the contents are blanked and the key pattern has no letter to start on. "Longer strings are blanked" keeps the quotes and blanks the contents, so the `,` or `)` the lookahead needs can never come from inside a string. The lookahead is zero-width, so the global scan resumes at the closing quote as before and the first-seen order and the de-duplication of `hookTextKeysAskedIn` are unchanged.
- Consumers: both save doors only iterate the returned keys and compare against `Object.keys(texts)`; neither depends on match offsets, so the change reaches them as a smaller key list and nothing else.

Docblocks, sentence by sentence: the section header ("the quote closing the argument ... a key built from a literal included"), the `TEXT_CALL` block and the `hookTextKeysAskedIn` block each say what the expression does. The retained `ctx.text!(` paragraph is still true.

- N1 (nit) — "literal" is syntactic, so a first argument that always evaluates to its literal but is not one token (`'key' || fallback`, `'key' ?? fallback`, `'key' + ''`) moves from the save refusal to the run-time refusal. The docblock's own definition covers it ("a literal joined to something"), the run-time fault names the key, and no author writes these on purpose. Accepted deviation; no change asked.

Read, not a finding on this diff (same on `main`, unchanged by it): a literal ask written inside a template hole, a parenthesised key `(('key'))`, and a literal fallback `ctx.text(k || 'key')` are not read at save and fall to the run-time refusal; and the masking has no notion of a regular-expression literal, so a quote inside one can shift the string scan. All four are in the direction of the run-time half, none is a false save refusal.

The dev's correction of the dispatch assumption (a template with a `${}` hole was already blanked by the masking, so never read as literal) is stated in the PR body and the report; those cases are pinned, not "fixed". The run-time half that now decides a built key exists and names the key (`undeclaredHookTextAtRun` / `undeclaredActionTextAtRun`, consumed by `packages/runtime/src/sandbox/hook-text.ts`). Both save doors read the one reader (`hook.zod.ts`, `action.zod.ts` → `hookTextKeysAskedIn` → `maskedSource` then `TEXT_CALL`), so the masking runs before the lookahead as the docblock says.
3. **Gates at this head (check-runs).** 58 success · 11 expected skip · 0 unexpected skip · 0 failed · 0 pending; Lint & Repo Gates and TypeScript Type Check both `success` (`l1-face.mjs --pr 36666`, clean on all 13 items). The dev's declared narrowing of local families (no spec build in a shared container) is covered by CI's run of every family at this head.
4. **Accepted deviations.** Tests: positive control present — the 10 dark `+`/member-access pins were red on the unfixed reader and turn red again under ablation of the lookahead, restored to the head blob. Rejection pins assert the exact save sentence at `body.source`; these are schema `safeParse` refusals, not HTTP envelopes, so the ADR-0112 `code`/`status` check does not apply. Changeset read sentence by sentence against the diff: true, with one nit accepted as is — "A key built from a literal is refused when the hook or action runs" means "when it is undeclared" (the paragraph before sets that context); no follow-up card.

6. **Landing.** Changeset `@objectstack/spec` patch present; no `content/docs/releases/` path; not governed (no governed path in the 4 files). Contract face: `packages/spec/src/data/hook-refusal-codes.ts` is the published-schema face, so an L2 at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is owed whatever the `Clause-②:` line says. L2 record: PR #36666 comment 7099600018 — `Served-tier: CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`, head `dc8f1abe60d3f9b070197b9f02a8ebf904401f95`, `Scope:` equals the `hits` (`hook-refusal-codes.ts`), tier verified on the reviewer's transcript, **PASS**, no must-fix or should-fix; its nit N1 (a first argument such as `'key' || fallback` now falls to the run-time refusal) is accepted as is.
